ru: Будь ку́хня побо́льше, мы бы гото́вили вме́сте.
en_alt: If the kitchen were bigger, we would cook together.
note: Imperfective conditional is correctly "would cook"; побольше is equally "bigger".

en_alt: Grandmother used to cook tasty pies.
note: The habitual reading of the imperfective past is equally valid.

ru: Весь ве́чер мы бу́дем гото́вить пра́здничный у́жин.

en_alt: Cook dinner, the guests will arrive soon.
note: "arrive" is the more idiomatic rendering of прийти here.

ru: Мы бу́дем гото́виться к экза́менам ско́ро.
К экза́мену она́ гото́вилась бы зара́нее.
note: Imperfective бы + past correctly reads as the present counterfactual "would prepare".

ru: Она́ гото́вилась к пое́здке весь день.
en_alt: She was preparing for the trip all day.
note: The progressive reading of the imperfective past is equally valid.

ru: Вы бы грози́ли ему́ и́з-за пустяка́?
en: Would you threaten him over a trifle?
en_alt: Would you threaten him over something so trivial?
note: "something so trivial" adds emphasis the Russian does not carry; пустяк is simply "a trifle".

ru: Я не грожу́, я про́сто предупрежда́ю.
en_alt: I am not threatening, I am simply warning.
note: просто is equally "simply".

en_alt: He shook his finger at me.
He wagged his finger at me.
note: грозить пальцем is a set gesture; the literal en_gb is understandable but the idiomatic renderings should be accepted too.
грози́ть гро́зой is a cognate tautology and the English "threatening a thunderstorm" reads oddly; a human should decide whether to reword (e.g. грози́ть дождём).

ru: Без неиспра́вности мото́р не гуде́л бы так.
note: Imperfective conditional correctly "wouldn't hum".

en_alt: The engine is humming outside.
note: на улице is very commonly just "outside".

en_alt: The bees are buzzing over the flowers.
note: "buzzing" is the natural English for bees; en_gb keeps the headword gloss.

ru: Без дождя́ де́ти гуля́ли бы до са́мого ве́чера.
en: Without the rain, the children would stay out until the very evening.
en_alt: If it were not raining, the children would stay out until the evening.
note: до са́мого ве́чера ("right up until evening") loses са́мого in the current English.

en_alt: Stroll in the park every day.
note: Adds the headword's own gloss as an accepted answer.

en_alt: Are you out walking with the dog?
note: "walking the dog" is the right idiom; the literal "with the dog" reading is worth accepting too.

ru: По́сле обе́да де́ти бу́дут гуля́ть в саду́.
en: After lunch the children will be walking in the garden.
en_alt: After lunch the children will be out in the garden.
note: "play" renders гуля́ть against its own gloss "to stroll" and imports an activity the Russian does not name.

en_alt: Are you strolling in the park?
note: The Russian present covers both the habitual and the ongoing reading.

en_alt: Are you strolling along the embankment?
note: The Russian present covers both the habitual and the ongoing reading.

ru: Он дава́л бы бо́льше, е́сли бы мог.
note: Imperfective side of the collision is correct as a present counterfactual "would give"; the perfective partner is the half being fixed.

en_alt: Let's begin the lesson.
note: нача́ть is equally "begin".

en_alt: She gives me a book.
note: The Russian present covers both the simple and the progressive reading.

en_alt: The teacher is giving us a task.
note: The Russian present covers both the simple and the progressive reading.

ru: Тепе́рь я бу́ду дава́ть тебе́ уро́ки му́зыки.

en_alt: His parents gave him money.
note: "used to give" is a fair imperfective rendering; the plain past should also be accepted.

ru: Ра́ньше он дари́л ей цветы́ ка́ждый день.
Что ты да́ришь ма́ме на пра́здник?
en_alt: What are you giving your mum for the holiday?
note: The Russian present also carries the near-future reading of a specific occasion.

en_alt: I am giving my mum flowers.
note: The Russian present covers both the simple and the progressive reading.

ru: При необходи́мости мы да́ли бы вам ещё оди́н день.
en: If it had been necessary, we would have given you one more day.
en_alt: If necessary, we would have given you one more day.
note: Perfective бы + past should read as a single completed event ("would have given"); as written it collides with the imperfective partner's "would give".

en_alt: Give me a pencil, please.
note: Word order variant, so the word-bank drill accepts both.

ru: За́втра коло́нна бу́дет дви́гаться на юг.

en_alt: The train was moving very slowly.
note: The progressive is the more characteristic reading of the imperfective past.

ru: Зна́я доро́гу, они́ дви́нулись бы ра́ньше.
en: Knowing the way, they would have set off earlier.
en_alt: Knowing the road, they would have set off earlier.
note: Perfective бы + past with ра́ньше is a past counterfactual about a single completed departure, so "would have set off".

en_alt: We will set out on our way in the morning.
note: дви́нуться в путь is "set out on the journey"; the fuller rendering keeps в путь visible.

en_alt: The train moved off from the station.
note: Matches the wording used for the future sibling sentence.

en_alt: She did not budge.
note: не дви́нуться с ме́ста is idiomatically "not budge"; the literal en_gb stays.

ru: В тако́й ситуа́ции она́ де́йствовала бы ина́че.
en_alt: In such a situation, she would act differently.
note: тако́й is "such a" rather than "that"; the imperfective conditional "would act" is right.

en_alt: One must act quickly.
It is necessary to act quickly.
note: The Russian is impersonal — "we" is supplied by English, so the subjectless renderings should be accepted.

en_alt: He is acting decisively.
note: The Russian present covers both the habitual and the ongoing reading.

en_alt: Are you acting decisively?
note: The Russian present covers both the habitual and the ongoing reading.

ru: В слу́чае опа́сности мы бу́дем де́йствовать бы́стро.
en_alt: In case of danger we will act quickly.
note: The plain future is the more natural English for this future imperfective.

en_alt: Do your lessons every day.
note: де́лать уро́ки is idiomatically "do homework"; the literal reading is worth accepting.
Past active participle rendered correctly as a relative clause.

en_alt: While doing his homework, he was listening to music.
note: The imperfective past also carries the progressive reading.

ru: Ты бу́дешь де́лать заря́дку ка́ждое у́тро?

en_alt: Are you doing your homework?
note: Determiner variant; both are natural for the bare Russian noun phrase.

en_alt: Do your exercises every morning.
note: Matches the wording of the ты бу́дешь sibling sentence.

en: What are you doing in the evening?
en_alt: What do you do in the evening?
note: "this evening" imports сего́дня, and duplicated the English of the sibling «Что ты де́лаешь сего́дня ве́чером?» exactly.

en_alt: They were doing everything correctly.
note: The progressive reading of the imperfective past is equally valid.

en_alt: Do you do your exercises in the mornings?
note: Determiner variant for заря́дку.

ru: Что бы вы де́лали на моём ме́сте?

en_alt: What do you do at weekends?
note: Both singular and plural render the Russian plural выходны́е naturally in en_gb.

en_alt: He was feeling worse and worse.
note: The dative subject makes this an experiencer construction; both readings are standard.

ru: Без све́та в ко́мнате де́лалось бы темно́.
en: Without light it would get dark in the room.
en_alt: Without light the room would get dark.
note: The Russian is impersonal (де́лалось бы темно́); promoting «комната» to subject hides the construction the sentence is teaching.
Here де́латься is the passive "are done", a sense the headword gloss "to become" does not cover — the gloss is probably the half that needs widening.
Same as the sibling: "is done" is outside the headword gloss "to become"; widening the gloss is likelier than changing the sentence.

ru: При тако́м ве́тре он держа́л бы зонт обе́ими рука́ми.
en_alt: In such a wind, he would hold the umbrella with both hands.
note: тако́м is "such a"; the imperfective conditional "would hold" is right.

en_alt: They were holding the door open.
note: The progressive reading of the imperfective past is equally valid.

ru: Отны́не я бу́ду держа́ть су́мку, а ты иди́.

en_alt: We were holding hands.
note: Idiomatic en_gb is right; the progressive should also be accepted.

ru: На э́том мосту́ я держа́лся бы за пери́ла.
note: Imperfective conditional correctly "would hold on".

ru: В по́езде я бу́ду держа́ться за по́ручень.
en_alt: On the train I will be holding on to the handrail.
note: Future imperfective also takes the progressive rendering.

en_alt: Add some milk, please.
note: Word order variant; the partitive genitive молока́ is correctly "some milk".

ru: Вы доба́вили бы в суп немно́го пе́рца?
note: Perfective бы here is a polite request, so "Would you add…" is correct rather than "would have added".

ru: Ско́ро по́вар доба́вит спе́ции в блю́до.

en_alt: I am trying to get an answer.
note: "pressing for" is accurate but not the headword gloss; the plainer rendering should also be accepted.

ru: С бо́льшей подде́ржкой она́ доби́лась бы лу́чшего результа́та.
en: With more support, she would have achieved a better result.
en_alt: With greater support, she would have achieved a better result.
note: Perfective бы + past about an already-obtained result is a past counterfactual — "would have achieved", which also keeps it distinct from imperfective добива́ться.

ru: На по́езде вы добра́лись бы туда́ быстре́е.
en_alt: You would have got there faster by train.
note: Perfective бы + past also supports the past-counterfactual reading; en_gb keeps the advice reading.

en_alt: We got home late.
note: "got home" is the everyday English for добра́ться до дома.

ru: По́сле тако́й лжи она́ ему́ не доверя́ла бы.
note: Imperfective conditional correctly "would not trust".

ru: Вы довели́ бы ребёнка до до́ма?
en_alt: Would you see the child home?
Would you take the child home?
note: довести́ до до́ма is accompanying on foot; "walk home" is fine, the alternatives should be accepted too.

en_alt: Will you see the matter through to the end?
note: довести́ де́ло до конца́ is the set phrase "see something through".

en_alt: He saw the matter through to the end.
note: Same set phrase as the ты sibling.

ru: Э́та доро́га доведёт нас до́ дома.
en_alt: This road will take us home.
note: Equally natural rendering of доведёт.

en_alt: I will take you as far as the corner.
note: до угла́ is "as far as the corner"; both are natural.

ru: Ско́ро тропи́нка доведёт нас до о́зера.
Ско́ро ты догада́ешься, в чём де́ло.
en_alt: Soon you will guess what the matter is.
note: в чём де́ло is literally "what the matter is"; the idiomatic en_gb stays.

en_alt: I guessed it all straight away.
note: сра́зу is equally "straight away".

ru: Без э́той подска́зки она́ не догада́лась бы.
note: Perfective бы + past already correctly rendered as "would not have guessed".
